dharana.numbering_edition: Jaideva Singh 1979 (dhāraṇā 1 = verse 24; dhāraṇā 82 = verses 105–106 and dhāraṇā 89 = verses 113–114, otherwise one verse each; dhāraṇā 112 = verse 137)
dharana.sanskrit_iast: samaḥ śatrau ca mitre ca samo mānāvamānayoḥ | brahmaṇaḥ paripūrṇatvād iti jñātvā sukhī bhavet ||
dharana.sanskrit_source: GRETIL e-text, compared with Wallis's concordance, Pradīpaka and the Singh scan
sanskrit_variants: verse 125: GRETIL prints a double daṇḍa at the half-verse and paripūrṇatvāt iti; corrected to paripūrṇatvād iti with Wallis and Pradīpaka.
dharana.rendering: Being the same toward enemy and friend, the same in honour and dishonour, knowing that brahman is full everywhere, one becomes happy.
dharana.rendering_attribution: School paraphrase drawing on Jaideva Singh (1979), Christopher Wallis and Bettina Bäumer (as printed in Wallis's concordance); not a quotation.
dharana.commentary_note: Singh: from the conviction that brahman is present everywhere comes equality of consciousness (samatā): the same goodwill toward all, neither elated by honour nor depressed by dishonour. He compares Bhagavad Gītā 5.18 and 14.25. Wallis: 'equal towards all'.
dharana.instruction: Meet friend and foe, praise and blame, with the same even mind.

checked_against: The Mystery Within (2019), Session Two list: 'Dharana 100' = verse 125 (agrees with Singh)
Wallis concordance: verse 125 = 'Equal towards all (Y100 ~ B3)' (verse text and technique match)
GRETIL, Wallis and Pradīpaka: Sanskrit of verse 125 compared
verification.notes: Door index = Singh dhāraṇā number, read directly in Singh's own headings and cross-checked against The Mystery Within's Singh-numbered list and Wallis's concordance. Caveat: Singh was read from an OCR scan, not a print copy in hand.

numbering_variants.mystery_within_parallel: The parallel-translations section of The Mystery Within labels verse 125 'Dharana 102', because from verse 106 on it gives every verse its own number (106 = 83 … 137 = 114). Singh and the same book's Session Two list put this at dhāraṇā 100. Not followed.

seat.label: Any steady, comfortable position (school addition)
seat.summary: Any steady, comfortable position: sitting on a chair, sitting on the floor with support under the hips, or lying on the back. Standing or walking slowly is also acceptable when that is easier. Choose the position in which the body needs the least effort.
seat.honesty: School addition. Verse 125 does not specify a body position. The seat is a convenience so the dharana can be practised; it is not part of the technique and makes no claim of tradition.

geometry.summary: Not a body shape. The map is a level balance with friend and foe, praise and blame on either side, held even by the fullness present in both.
geometry.svg_hint: a level balance beam with equal marks on each side
geometry.honesty: Geometry records the dharana's own map of attention, not a body shape. Locations marked 'commentarial' come from commentary, not from the verse.

reaction.name: Hold it level
reaction.summary: School metaphor only: the mind stops tilting toward friends and praise and away from foes and blame, and rests level. Not a biochemical or medical claim.

breath.lands_in: wherever the breath naturally ends; this door places nothing on the breath
breath.cue: Natural breath. Count about four in and four out only if it helps you settle, then let the count go. No forced hold.
breath.honesty: The counts are an optional school pacing aid, not part of the verse. Hold is always 0: this school never adds a deliberate breath-hold.

orientation.cue: Bring to mind friend and foe, praise and blame, and stay level
orientation.gravity: Let the floor or chair carry the body completely; there is no posture to hold
orientation.degrees_hint: No angle target: the VBT gives no posture for this dharana

attention.primary: The same attitude toward friend and foe, praise and blame

adiyogi.verse_paraphrase: Being the same toward enemy and friend, the same in honour and dishonour, knowing that brahman is full everywhere, one becomes happy.
adiyogi.method_summary: Bring to mind someone you like and someone you find difficult; a moment of praise and a moment of blame. Recognise the same fullness present in each, and let the mind settle level, leaning toward neither. Carry that evenness into the day.

honesty.disclosure: Door 100 follows Vijñāna Bhairava Tantra dharana 100 (verse 125) in Jaideva Singh's numbering. The door-to-dharana index is a School of 112 Doorways teaching device. Singh's sequence is one edition's count, not an ancient one-to-one canon. The seat, counts, reaction and beat scripts are school additions.
honesty.notes: pairing_type is school_device: the dharana is the content, while the door index, seat and pacing are the school's.
flags: Door index = Jaideva Singh dharana number: Door 100 is dharana 100, verse 125. Other editions number differently (see dharana.numbering_variants).
The seat, breath counts, reaction metaphor, attention-map drawing and beat scripts are school devices, not part of the verse.
The English is a school paraphrase, not a quotation from any translator.
No medical claims. Reaction names are metaphors, not biochemistry.
New door researched on 2026-10-06 on branch research/vbt-houses-2-7; awaiting guardian review.

safety.pain_rule: Pain is information. Pause, regress, or exit. Never push through sharp pain.
safety.open_seat_alternate: This door needs no particular posture: sit on a chair, sit on the floor with support, or lie down. Eyes may stay open.
safety.contraindication_notes: General practice caution only; not medical advice. Equanimity does not mean accepting harm: keep your boundaries, and step away from people or situations that are unsafe. If anything feels distressing (dizziness, agitation, strong emotion), stop, open the eyes and rest attention on the feet and the floor.

beats.title: Name the door
beats.script: This is Door 100: equal toward friend and foe. Vijñāna Bhairava Tantra dharana 100, verse 125.

beats.title: Geometry
beats.script: No shape to make. Sit, or carry this into the day. The map is a level balance: friend and foe, praise and blame.

beats.title: Orientation
beats.script: Let the floor or the chair carry you. Eyes closed or soft.

beats.title: Breath
beats.script: Natural breath. Count about four in and four out only if it helps. No forced hold.

beats.title: Attention
beats.script: Bring to mind a friend, then someone difficult. A moment of praise, then of blame. The same fullness in each. Stay level.

beats.title: Reaction cue
beats.script: School image: a balance held level. A metaphor, not medicine.

beats.title: Adiyogi thread
beats.script: Verse 125: the same toward enemy and friend, honour and dishonour, knowing brahman is full everywhere, one becomes happy.

beats.title: Exit / integrate
beats.script: Take a slow, free breath. Carry the level mind into your next meeting with someone.
